doc.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022

title: Learning to splice tape
summary: His first tape splice on a Paul Winter date and how tape editing compares with Pro Tools.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Do you recall the first time you were asked to splice tape?

I do. Yeah actually, yeah. It was an 8 track recording, I think it was Paul Winter I think was the artist actually. And I was assisting on the date. And the engineer said, “Yeah put that together.” You know like that. “Put some splicing tape, and put that together.” And I thought oh man. So, and you do it. You do it, like any other craft you just learn how to do it.
You observe and listen and then —
Yeah. I don’t think I’d want to practice on a real date you know, but —

You know it’s funny, those were the techniques in those days, so you didn’t think much about it. I mean subsequently there would be edits that I would attempt to do, and hopefully successfully, that required, you know, slices of a piece of tape. And you might have three or four different tries at it that were all sliced and you’d have to get them in order on the backing with the tape backing so they would play correctly. Because if it didn’t play then you just destroyed something. So you learned these editing techniques. It’s a little easier today with Pro Tools and Logic Audio, a little less nerves going on.
